skill.description: Guides developers building Alkahest escrow integrations with TypeScript, Rust, and Python SDK examples.
skill.summary: Build Alkahest escrow, obligation, arbiter, and payment flows across supported SDKs.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown or SDK reference false positives, including code fences, TypeScript template literal types, and blockchain UID fields. The audit confirms repeated inline private-key placeholders in setup examples as a real copy-paste safety risk for wallet code. No prompt injection, data-exfiltration intent, or unauthorized command execution evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Inline private-key placeholders appear in setup examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace literal private-key arguments with environment-variable or secret-manager examples, and add a warning against committing wallet keys.

remediation.issue: RPC URLs are shown as literal placeholders in client setup.
remediation.suggestion: State that RPC endpoints are user-provided configuration values and should not include committed credentials.

content.value_statement: Developers need clear guidance for Alkahest escrow, fulfillment, and arbiter workflows. This skill organizes SDK patterns for TypeScript, Rust, and Python.
actual_capabilities: Explains client setup for TypeScript, Rust, and Python Alkahest SDKs.
Shows escrow creation, fulfillment, collection, and wait-for-fulfillment flows.
Maps SDK types across TypeScript, Rust, and Python.
Documents arbiter demand encoding, commit-reveal obligations, and atomic payment helpers.
Provides contract address and schema reference material for supported networks.
limitations: The Python reference notes that it still describes a legacy SDK surface.
It is documentation only and does not verify live contract deployments.
Examples use placeholder private keys and RPC URLs that users must replace securely.
It does not provide automated tests or runnable project scaffolding.

use_cases.title: Add Escrow Payments to an App
use_cases.description: Use SDK patterns to create token escrows, fulfill obligations, and collect payments.

use_cases.title: Compare SDK Surfaces
use_cases.description: Translate Alkahest concepts across TypeScript, Rust, and Python before choosing an implementation language.

use_cases.title: Design Arbiter Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan trusted oracle, logical arbiter, attestation property, and commit-reveal demand flows.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Client Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to configure an Alkahest TypeScript client for Base Sepolia. Include safe handling for wallet keys and RPC URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Escrow Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist for building an ERC20 escrow flow with Alkahest in Rust. Cover approval, escrow creation, fulfillment, and collection.

prompt_templates.title: Compare SDK APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the TypeScript, Rust, and Python Alkahest SDK APIs for string obligations and commit-reveal obligations.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Arbiter Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a commit-reveal fulfillment workflow for an Alkahest escrow. Include demand encoding, deadlines, bond handling, and failure cases.

output_examples.input: Create an ERC20 escrow integration plan for a TypeScript app.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan covering wallet setup, approval, escrow creation, fulfillment tracking, collection, and security checks.

output_examples.input: Compare Rust and Python support for Alkahest commit-reveal obligations.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of method names, return types, data encoding, and the Python reference currency warning.

output_examples.input: Explain which arbiter fits an oracle-reviewed job marketplace.
output_examples.output: A recommendation that compares trusted oracle and logical arbiter flows, with notes on demand data and attestation references.

best_practices: Store private keys in a secure secret manager or environment variable outside source control.
Verify contract addresses and chain configuration before sending transactions.
Start on test networks and confirm escrow lifecycle events before mainnet use.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding wallet private keys or RPC credentials in application source.
Copying placeholder addresses without checking the target network.
Using legacy Python examples without checking current SDK compatibility.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps developers use Alkahest SDKs to build escrow, fulfillment, arbiter, and payment workflows.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers TypeScript, Rust, and Python SDK patterns, with contract reference material.

faq.question: Does it include runnable project files?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples, not a complete project scaffold.

faq.question: Can it help with contract addresses?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes reference tables for supported Alkahest contract deployments.

faq.question: Is the Python reference current?
faq.answer: The Python reference states that it describes a legacy SDK surface and needs follow-up.

faq.question: How should private keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use a secure secret manager or environment variable, and never commit wallet keys to source control.
